Darsuniskis Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kauno apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Darsūniškis's Jewish population never exceeded 300–350 even at its peak, falling to about 120 by the interwar period; most worked in petty trade, labor, and peddling. Following the German occupation in 1941, a ghetto was established, and on August 15, all Jewish men were led toward Kaunas by armed Lithuanians and murdered; the remaining 99 people — 69 women, 20 children, and 10 elderly or sick men — were massacred directly at this cemetery between August 28 and September 2, 1941. A memorial was erected here in 1991 through the initiative of the local council.
